fields.meta_title: Service Request Form Builder With Routing | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a service request form that puts safety repairs first and checks warranty dates on submit. Every request lands in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Service Request Form That Sorts Requests on Arrival
fields.hero_description: Describe your services and the rules your team follows. Emergent builds the service request form, sorts each request by its answers and keeps every one in a table.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Does After Submit
fields.features_subheading: A blank template records the request and stops there. These six pieces decide who picks it up and how soon.
fields.feature_1:
Services from your own menu

List every service you take requests for, each with its own follow-up questions. A brake complaint asks about the noise, and a new laptop asks for the role and start date.
fields.feature_2:
Rules that set the priority

Mark the answers that make a request urgent, such as a safety symptom or a stopped production line. Those requests move up on submit, and the rest wait in order of arrival.
fields.feature_3:
Photos and receipts on upload

Add an upload field for a picture of the fault or a proof of purchase. The file sits on the request record, where the technician sees it before driving out to the customer.
fields.feature_4:
Routing by service area or team

Send each request to the person who covers that ZIP code or that department. When someone is away for the week, reassign their open requests in one step from the dashboard.
fields.feature_5:
Status emails the customer reads

Email the customer when the request is scheduled and again when it is closed, with the date and the name of whoever is coming. Fewer people phone in to ask where it stands.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your repository

Export the full codebase to GitHub when you want the request form inside your own customer portal, or running on the servers that your own team already manages and patches.

fields.tab_content_1:
Four teams get their tasks from one new-hire request

Northwind Logistics starts new hires on Mondays. A sales manager submits one request for Ana Ruiz with her role and start date. The form turns it into four tasks: a laptop for IT, a CRM seat for sales ops, a badge for facilities and a desk for the office manager. Each task is due the Wednesday before she starts.
fields.tab_content_2:
Brake symptoms jump ahead of every oil change

Ridgeline Auto keeps the first bay of each morning open. When a customer picks Brakes or Steering as the symptom, the request is marked Safety and gets the 7:30 AM slot the next day. An oil change books into the next open slot that week. Both customers get a confirmation email with their time.
fields.tab_content_3:
Purchase date decides who pays for the visit

Brightline Appliance Repair asks for the purchase date and a photo of the receipt next to the model number. A washer bought 8 months ago is inside the 12-month warranty window. The visit books at no charge. An older machine shows the $95 diagnostic fee on screen before the customer submits.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every termite call starts with an inspection

Hollis Pest Control never quotes termites over the phone. A request that names termites books a free inspection with Reggie Dawson, the termite inspector, since the treatment depends on what he finds. Ants and rodents go to the technician who covers that ZIP code.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Service Request Form
fields.howto_description: Settle which requests you take and what each one needs before you open the builder.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for the proof you will need
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each service a customer or an employee can ask for, in the words they would use. Give each one its own short set of questions. A laptop request and a furnace repair should never share one path through the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Go through each question and mark the answers that change what happens next. A safety symptom moves a job up the schedule. A purchase date settles who pays. Everything else is information for the technician, not a rule.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add upload fields for whatever saves a second trip, such as the receipt or a shot of the error code. Make them required only where the visit fails without them. Keep the rest optional so people finish the form.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Map every service to a person or a team, and to a service area if you cover more than one. Pick a backup for each person. Requests then keep moving when someone is on vacation or out sick.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put your services, rules and routing into one prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form along with the requests table your team works from. As your services change, ask for the change in the same chat.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect a calendar so bookings land on the right day, and email so customers get their confirmations. Anything else with an API, such as an invoicing tool, can receive a new request or a closed one.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Submit one request of each kind
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the form on a phone the way a customer would, once for each service. Check that the urgent request moves to the front, and that every request reaches the person who should handle it.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is split between downloadable templates (Smartsheet Word, Excel and PDF files, Cognito Forms, Jotform), one shared Microsoft Forms instance, two county clerk forms, Adobe's list of fields to include and a how-to video. Every one of them stops at the fields. This page answers the definition and how-to questions directly, then shows what a service request form decides after submit in four service businesses: a new-hire setup split across three teams, safety repairs moved to the front of a shop's schedule, warranty status settled by purchase date, and termite calls sent to an inspector before any treatment is sold.
tab_stories: A hiring manager at Northwind Logistics requests setup for a sales hire who starts Monday, and the one request becomes laptop, email and badge tasks for three teams, each due the Wednesday before.
A Ridgeline Auto customer picks Brakes as the symptom, so the request is marked Safety and offered the 7:30 AM bay tomorrow, while an oil change gets the next open slot later in the week.

A Brightline Appliance Repair customer enters a washer bought 8 months ago with a photo of the receipt, and the request books as a warranty visit at no charge, while a 3-year-old dryer shows the $95 diagnostic fee before submit.

Hollis Pest Control reads the pest type on each request, sends every termite request to its licensed inspector for a free inspection first, and routes ants, rodents and wasps to the technician who covers that ZIP code.

claims_to_source: In ITIL, a service request is a user asking for information, advice or access to a service
In ITIL, an incident is an issue or degradation of a service that is affecting the user, which is different from a service request
Common IT service requests include password resets, software installations, hardware requests, access permissions and account creations
A request for service form typically asks for the requester's name, contact information and the type of service requested
